case.description: laminar mixed convection, vertical pipe, buoyancy-assisting, constant wall heat flux

truth_independence.open_issue: prior implementation marked this substrate divergent_truth_substrate=False; unresolved

lock_stages.REVISED: an earlier ordering put the grid and surrogate in the first lock, to be fixed BEFORE the measurement inventory. Both depend on knowing which measured conditions exist, so that ordering fixed them in ignorance.
lock_stages.invariant: lock every SCORING choice before any label, flag or performance number is examined. Nothing more is required.

lock_A.covers: result vocabulary, materiality definition and refused provenances, flag rule, truth-independence requirements, baselines

unlocked_work.covers: source discovery, input-only inventory, rebuilt CFD, matched gravity-off runs, surrogate fitting and verification
unlocked_work.note: these produce inputs, not scoring choices, so they need no freeze -- only the discipline of recording inputs not outcomes

lock_B.covers: grid and evaluable rule, surrogate FORM AND SPLIT, label rule and tolerance, theta, metric definitions, corroboration criterion
lock_B.when: after the inventory, and before materiality or fit residuals are inspected at any evaluation condition

neutrality.principle: not everything preceding a label is a neutral input
neutral_may_inspect_before_lock_B: source inventory: conditions, geometry, stated uncertainty
CFD grid convergence, residuals, energy balance
NOT_neutral_must_not_inspect_before_lock: surrogate fit residual at an evaluation condition
neutrality.why: through the coupling E = d - m(1+d) + eps, materiality and the fit residual at a condition both carry information about that condition's eventual error label. Seeing either before the scoring choices are fixed is seeing a shadow of the answer, even though neither is itself a label.

condition_sets.development: for choosing the surrogate's functional form. Residuals here MAY be inspected before Lock B. These conditions are then SPENT and take no part in the evaluation -- not held out, discarded.
condition_sets.fit: fitting the final surrogate once the form is fixed
condition_sets.evaluation: scoring. Untouched until Lock B is recorded.

must_record: measurement sources: publication, table or figure, digitisation method
available operating points with their (Re, Gr*)
eligibility under the section 1 evaluable rule, with a reason per point
whether each eligible point carries a stated uncertainty, and its source
the redistribution determination for each source
must_not_record: trustworthy / untrustworthy labels or their counts
class balance, or any count derived from comparing predictions against truth
measurement_inventory.why: labels and flags are OUTCOMES: the label rule applied to predictions, truth and uncertainty, and the flag rule applied to calibration and materiality. Seeing them before the stage-2 lock means choosing the criterion knowing which way it falls.

result_vocabulary.reproduced_means: a close rerun of the original evaluation: same grid, same truth source, same counterfactual
result_vocabulary.reproduced_unreachable_because: the original inputs are gone; this reconstruction necessarily changes the grid, the truth source and the counterfactual
result_vocabulary.matching_result_is_called: independent corroboration of the causal finding
result_vocabulary.rejected_test: containment of the original value in the reconstruction's confidence interval. A value inside an interval is a failure to reject, not a demonstration of agreement; a wide enough interval contains almost anything. Equivalence requires a margin and a test against it, and the margin cannot be chosen before the measurements are known.
result_vocabulary.removed_proposals: min evaluable points = 12 and max interval width = 0.35, both withdrawn as numbers picked in ignorance of the data

outcomes.CORROBORATED: independently supports the causal finding under the stage-2 criterion
outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: available measurements cannot support a metric claim either way

invariants: metrics are always reported with their uncertainty, never as bare point estimates
the numbers presented are the reconstruction's; the original triple is never presented as a number this repository produces
result_vocabulary.consistent_with: known-results-declaration.md; neither may change without the other

original_construction.surrogate: forced-convection closure Nu_forced(Re) fitted to the gravity-off CFD; implementing code did not survive
original_construction.truth: Mohammed & Salman assisting-flow correlation Eq 13, evaluated densely

shared_input_coupling.relation: E = d - m(1+d) + eps, with E the relative surrogate error and m the materiality
shared_input_coupling.effect: for small d and eps the label rule |E| > tol approaches the flag condition m >= theta; with theta ~= tol a flagged point is labelled untrustworthy
shared_input_coupling.status: mechanism established; NOT established as an identity
conditional_on: step 4 error scale: UNKNOWN (scale is an undefined symbol in the surviving design)
surrogate fit residual eps: UNRECOVERABLE (no coefficients, R2 or residual survive)
sign of d across the grid: NOT ESTABLISHED (two observations, both Ri >= 1.8)
shared_input_coupling.false_positives_remain_possible_when: eps is positive and large enough to offset d - m(1+d); >= +3.3% just above theta under the observed d, rising past +20% at m = 0.26
shared_input_coupling.inversion: recovering precision ~= 1.00 in the reconstruction would be evidence the coupling survived, not evidence the method works

original_construction.grid_bounds_source: https://pure.kfupm.edu.sa/en/publications/heat-transfer-measurements-of-mixed-convection-for-upward-and-dow/ -- Re 400-1600, Gr 1.1e5-7.4e6; matches the step-4 grid. An earlier overrun claim was withdrawn: it used the companion ECM paper's ranges by mistake
original_construction.envelope_vs_coverage: grid bounds lying inside the experimental range does NOT establish measurement coverage at grid points; the evaluable rule must address coverage

source_paper.citation: Mohammed, H. A. & Salman, Y. K. (2008). Experimental Heat Transfer 21(1):1-23
source_paper.test_run_coverage: 4 entrance lengths (L/D 20/40/60/80) x upward and downward

measurement_uncertainty.note: single global maximum; no per-condition band is reported

source_paper.CORRECTION: the +/-8% figure this project carried as experimental uncertainty is the scatter of the data about the fitted correlation (paper: 'the overall accuracy of heat transfer data in these correlations ... of the order of +/-8%, as shown in Figure 16'). The MEASUREMENT uncertainty on Nu is +/-1.27%. Do not use 8% as measurement uncertainty.

individual_values.figure_16: Log Nu vs Log Ra/Re, Re 400-1600, Gr 1.1e5-7.4e6 -- the average-Nu data the correlation was fitted through
individual_values.recovery_method: exact extraction of marker coordinates from the PDF content stream; axis calibration is the only error source. NOT visual digitisation.

source_paper.label_rule_entanglement: truth choice determines which uncertainty enters the label rule: 1.27% for a measured value, 8% for a correlation. A THIRD term, plot-extraction error, is not yet quantified and could dominate. NO claim is made about whether the second condition binds.

extraction.earlier_extraction_was_wrong: a first pass reported 40 markers in two classes of 20 and guessed they were upward and downward. They were the Sieder & Tate triangles and Brown & Gauvin circles. The present-work markers sit in a second coordinate space at 4.1677x scale that the first pass discarded.
extraction.recorded_ambiguity: the paper states 88 runs over 4 entrance lengths and both directions (~44 upward). 63 distinct upward markers does not reconcile with 44, and the caption calls the figure 'a sample one of these correlations'. Entrance length per point is UNKNOWN.
extraction.redistribution_determination: NOT MADE; extraction held outside the repository

marker_count.why: the path count overcounts (markers drawn more than once; no threshold reconciles it) and the visual count undercounts (overlapped stars read as one blob). Distinct plotted measurements lie somewhere between ~23 and 81.
marker_count.EARLIER_FIGURE_WITHDRAWN: 63 was reported as the count; it is one clustering threshold's answer, not the count

why: Figure 16's x is a RATIO: a correct Ra/Re does not determine Re and Gr separately -- many (Re, Gr) pairs share one ratio
entrance length L/D is not recoverable per point; the figure aggregates four
without (Re, Gr, L/D) a point cannot be matched to a CFD condition
evaluable_cases.note: a marker count, however accurate, is not a case count

dependency_on_cfd.chain: measured points -> Eq 13 -> CFD accepted (and revised) against Eq 13 -> g-off CFD = Nu_F -> surrogate fitted to Nu_F
dependency_on_cfd.acceptance_criterion: agreement with Eq 13, to within the correlation's own +/-8% band
dependency_on_cfd.consequence: scoring that surrogate against these points is a CONSISTENCY CHECK, not an independent validation, unless the acceptance criterion is changed to one that does not reference Eq 13
dependency_on_cfd.precision_note: the step-3 Nusselt-extraction change is recorded as fixing a physical breakdown under outlet recirculation, not as a response to disagreement with Eq 13; which drove it is not separately recorded

correlation_discrepancy.status: UNRESOLVED -- the figure's axis, the plotted-data mapping, or the presentation of the correlation. At least one is inconsistent with the others. NO explanation is chosen; evidence does not select one.
correlation_discrepancy.WITHDRAWN_INFERENCE: an earlier entry inferred the CFD may have used a wrong Eq-13 argument and that its agreement could be coincidental. WITHDRAWN -- not supported. It compared against the figure's printed axis rather than against the physics, and the axis is itself the thing in question.

cfd_arguments_are_plausible.derivation: Ra/Re = Ri*Re*Pr; the CFD's own Re, Gr and Pr do NOT survive, only Ri, so these are derived by inversion, not recomputed from inputs
cfd_arguments_are_plausible.caveat: this does NOT prove Eq 13 or the CFD is correct; it only removes the wrong-argument inference

what_remains_unresolved.x_values: figure axis reads 1e6-1e8; physically available Ra/Re is 50-13,000
what_remains_unresolved.slope: plotted upward line rises ~3.5% across the figure; Eq 13 would rise ~75%
what_remains_unresolved.rescaling_ruled_out: a constant axis rescaling shifts x without changing slope. Implied exponent is 0.0063 on the physical range versus Eq 13's 0.11868

source_paper.standing_limitation: the CFD was compared with a FITTED CORRELATION, not with measured points. Unchanged by any measurement question above.
source_paper.figure_16_closed_as_a_route: Figure 16 is a correlation plot, not a pointwise benchmark. Its x is a ratio so Re and Gr cannot be separated; entrance length is not recoverable per point across four aggregated L/D; the distinct-marker count is indeterminate between ~23 and 81. Marker recovery abandoned.

cfd_acceptance.criteria: grid convergence, residuals, energy balance, sensitivity of the Nusselt extraction -- the CFD's own terms
cfd_acceptance.eq13_role: a REPORTED correlation check, not the acceptance test
cfd_acceptance.rationale: the original acceptance was agreement with Eq 13 within the correlation's own scatter band, which makes the measured points that Eq 13 is fitted through non-independent of the CFD

if_no_evaluable_truth_set: report a reproducible demonstration of the method -- rebuilt CFD with recorded numerical checks, matched ablation runs, and a surrogate with a measured generalisation residual -- with NO performance metrics attached

brown_gauvin_I.citation: Brown, C.K. & Gauvin, W.H. (1965). Combined free-and-forced convection: I. Heat transfer in aiding flow. Can. J. Chem. Eng. 43(6):306-312
brown_gauvin_I.direction: aiding -- correct direction for the NAFEMS case
brown_gauvin_I.access: closed; Wiley terms of use; no open copy; no abstract available
brown_gauvin_I.wall_boundary_condition: CONSTANT WALL TEMPERATURE -- differs from Mohammed & Salman's constant heat flux
brown_gauvin_I.reason: a constant-temperature wall and a constant-flux wall are different boundary-value problems, and L/D differs. NOT interchangeable with Mohammed & Salman.
brown_gauvin_I.per_run_data_uncertainty: UNKNOWN -- cannot be determined without obtaining the paper. It is a 1965 paper, so a stated per-run uncertainty may simply not exist.

lewis_1992.citation: Lewis, J. S. (1992). Combined free and forced convection heat transfer to water in a vertical tube. PhD thesis, City University London.
lewis_1992.access: open access; LICENCE NOT STATED on the record page
lewis_1992.redistribution_determination: MADE. The record page states no licence, but the PDF cover sheet carries the City Research Online policy: full items usable for personal research, educational or NOT-FOR-PROFIT purposes with attribution and a link, content unchanged. We redistribute transcribed NUMBERS, not the document; *.pdf is gitignored and none has ever been tracked. Note the policy is narrower than this repo's CC BY 4.0, which permits commercial use.
lewis_1992.wall_boundary_condition: uniform heat flux -- MATCHES the NAFEMS case's BC
lewis_1992.working_fluid: water (the NAFEMS case is air; this is a different fluid)
lewis_1992.which: 35A only. The other 29 exist as Figures 6.7-6.13, not as numbers.
lewis_1992.cases_not_observations: One operating run is ONE case. 35A's 12 axial stations are 12 measurements of the same condition, not 12 independent cases. Counting them as cases would inflate any metric.

screens_applied.energy_balance: 35A carries -3.96%, worse than the 30-run median of 2.32%. 12 runs fall within 2%; 35A is not one of them.
screens_applied.flow_reversal: PREDICTED by Lewis's own code, Table 7.1, for 6 conditions. 35A is NOT among them: Lewis states no reversal was predicted for the Figure 7.4 group (Re 1098-1181). 35A's Gr_q/Re = 328 is below every tabulated entry. Predicted, not measured.
screens_applied.fluctuations: Recorded only in separate Tests 36-43, NOT in the main series. Qualitative: larger and more irregular in the upper half of the tube; Lewis calls the measurements 'of only a preliminary nature'.
screens_applied.stations_lewis_discounts: x/d 0.31 and 0.85 (axial wall conduction; wall at x=0 measured 0.5-5.7 degC above inlet bulk) and x/d 159.33 ('suspect', flange heat loss). 9 of 12 stations on 35A survive.

components: flow rate +/-1.2% (9 of 12 checks), run fluctuation +/-1.5%
voltage and current each +/-1% of data-logger value
thermocouple correction +0.13 K (ice) to +0.56 K (steam), applied
RTD probe-to-probe < 0.1 K, but NEVER TRACEABLY CALIBRATED
local wall heat generation -4% to +1% of average; +/-3.5% in Test 15A
per_point_uncertainty.ruling: Constructible by propagation, not reported. Building one is a modelling choice with real freedom in it and must be fixed in this protocol BEFORE any label, flag or metric is computed.

lewis_1992.status: experimental evaluation CANDIDATE. Not an evaluable set.

hallman_1961.citation: Hallman, T. M. (1961). Experimental Study of Combined Forced and Free Laminar Convection in a Vertical Tube. NASA TN D-1104.
hallman_1961.geometry: vertical circular tube, water, uniform wall heat flux, aiding AND opposing
hallman_1961.why_it_matters: It does what Lewis does not: separates its steady runs from its unsteady ones. 'The data which are believed to be fully developed and which were steady (nonfluctuating) are shown in figure 9.'
hallman_1961.stated_uncertainty: Nu = 6.12 +/- 0.25, about 4%, from a detailed error analysis on run U50
hallman_1961.blocker: No run table. Conditions are in Hallman's 1958 Purdue thesis, not reachable. Per-run Re and Pr would have to be digitised from figure abscissae.
hallman_1961.correlation_does_not_transfer_to_lewis: Lewis's stations sit at Re*Pr/(2x/D) = 30 to 488, from 1.5x to 24x outside the validated range. The extrapolation is permissive and contradicts the direct observation that 13A's measured Nu exceeds laminar prediction by 34% at x/d 135.84. Applying it would be using a correlation outside its calibration -- the failure this project detects. NOT USED.
hallman_1961.status: candidate; geometry is the best match found

barozzi_1993.citation: Barozzi, G. S. (1993). Combined convection and other effects in heat transfer in horizontal flows. PhD thesis, City University London.
barozzi_1993.access: open; same City Research Online policy as Lewis
barozzi_1993.geometry: HORIZONTAL circular duct, water, uniform peripheral heating -- buoyancy acts ACROSS the flow, driving secondary circulation rather than aiding acceleration. A different mechanism from the NAFEMS case.
barozzi_1993.runs: 10 named (PA-PE, FA-FE) with entry and exit Re, Pr, Ra_q, Gr_q tabulated
barozzi_1993.measured: local Nu at 12 axial stations, reduction rule stated
barozzi_1993.steadiness_evidence: QUANTIFIED, and the strongest found: four measurement cycles at 2-5 minute intervals agreeing within 0.1 degC, maximum deviation from their average within 0.03 degC, and wall temperature variations randomly signed. An accepted sequence is reproduced.
barozzi_1993.stated_uncertainty: +/-16% at 95% coverage generally, rising to +/-28% near the entrance
barozzi_1993.caveats: Temporal steadiness is MEASURED; laminarity is argued from Re <= ~1000 plus an assumed Ra_q ~ 6e5 stability limit. Runs FC and FD sit at Ra_q ~ 5e6, about 8x above it, with Nu rising downstream.
barozzi_1993.verified: read directly -- title, institution and the steadiness criterion checked
barozzi_1993.status: closest complete package; the open question is whether horizontal cross-flow buoyancy tests the same thing. That is the owner's call.
barozzi_1993.ruling: NOT a substitute for the vertical aiding-flow case. Horizontal geometry puts buoyancy across the flow, driving secondary circulation instead of aiding acceleration -- a different mechanism. Retained as a SEPARATE GENERALIZATION VEHICLE, not as NAFEMS truth.

barozzi_dumas_collins_1984.citation: Barozzi, G. S., Dumas, A. & Collins, M. W. (1984). Sharp entry and transition effects for laminar combined convection of water in vertical tubes. Int. J. Heat and Fluid Flow 5(4):235-241.
barozzi_dumas_collins_1984.why_it_is_the_highest_value_item: Vertical tube, water, aiding flow -- the target geometry -- and its abstract reports a TRANSITION CRITERION DERIVED FROM MEASURED LOCAL Nu. That is precisely the screen missing everywhere else: Lewis's criterion is from a laminar-only code, and Hallman's does not transfer.
barozzi_dumas_collins_1984.note: This is the correct citation for what earlier notes called 'Barozzi, Dumas & Stieglitz (1984)'.
barozzi_dumas_collins_1984.verified: NOT verified -- citation from a literature sweep
barozzi_dumas_collins_1984.status: obtain before settling for a horizontal-geometry compromise

lewis_case_choices.scope: Applies to the Lewis (1992) track ONLY. Kept entirely separate from the historical NAFEMS causal metrics, which concern a different fluid, geometry and experiment.

property_basis.reason: it is the basis on which Lewis prints the local Nu table, Table 7.1 and Figures 7.1-7.4
property_basis.sensitivity: the basis moves Re by 24% (1143 -> 1417) and Gr_q by 2.6x. Not interchangeable.
property_basis.beta_note: explicit input to the case generator, not derived. Mean-bulk beta is 2.23e-4, a factor 1.76 and the single largest lever on Gr_q.

qoi.choice: Nu(x) on a LINEAR energy-balance bulk temperature
qoi.bulk_endpoints: measured inlet 13.06 degC to CALCULATED exit 30.00 degC (not the measured exit, 29.32 degC)
qoi.how_settled: arithmetic, not assumption: reproducing the printed (Tw-Tb) at x/d=159.33 gives 29.06 K with the calculated exit and 29.73 K with the measured one; the printed value is 29.06 K. Lewis separately states the measured exit was 'not used for the evaluation of experimental Nusselt numbers'.
qoi.verification: the full rule reproduces all 12 printed Nu values
qoi.mixing_cup_is_a_different_quantity: Lewis's own PREDICTION code integrates a true mixing-cup bulk (Appendix F, SUMUCT loop). His EXPERIMENT uses the linear rise. Two different bulk definitions on the two sides of his own comparison. The rebuilt case reports both so they are never silently swapped.

flow_reversal_criterion.choice: per-cell: any cell with negative axial velocity, matching Lewis's 'the axial position where negative values of the axial velocity first appeared'
flow_reversal_criterion.rejected: net axial flux across a section. Mass conservation keeps it positive whatever the profile does, so it can never detect a reversal. An earlier version of cfd/compare_lewis.py used it and reported a meaningless 0.
flow_reversal_criterion.outlet_artifact_rule: a reversal confined to the FINAL axial row is an outlet boundary artifact, not a developing buoyancy reversal, and is reported as such rather than as a bare count.

cfd_acceptance.basis: the CFD's own numerical terms: operating-point match, grid convergence, energy closure, residual behaviour. NOT agreement with the experiment.
cfd_acceptance.why: the same rule as the NAFEMS case: accepting a CFD because it agrees with the measurement it is about to be tested against destroys the independence.

metrics_position.reason: No source yet supplies individually identified conditions, measured heat transfer AND positive evidence of steady laminar flow. Lewis supplies the first two; its well-measured runs are the transitional ones and its laminar run has the weakest buoyancy.
metrics_position.what_would_open_it: An eligible set of INDEPENDENT CASES -- distinct operating runs, not axial stations of one run -- each with measured truth, a stated uncertainty, and evidence the flow was steady and laminar where measured.
metrics_position.lewis_disposition: RETAINED as a documented limitation, not deleted.

development_vs_evaluation_split.the_error_being_corrected: The 13A laminar cutoff near x/d 102 was located by looking at WHERE MEASUREMENT AND PREDICTION DIVERGE. That is a legitimate diagnostic and it is how the constant-property defect was found. It cannot afterwards define a scoring region: a boundary drawn where agreement fails selects for agreement inside it, so any metric computed there is biased upward by construction.
development_vs_evaluation_split.what_burned_means: These three runs, every station of them, and the Figure 7.4 prediction curves have all been inspected against agreement. They may be used to build and debug the solver, and to argue about mechanisms. They may NOT contribute to any precision, recall, F1 or materiality figure, and no eligibility rule may be tuned on them.

rules_for_the_evaluation_set.order: Eligibility and QoI rules are fixed and committed FIRST. Only then is agreement computed, and only on runs not in the burned list.
forbidden_inputs_when_fixing_the_rules: measurement-versus-prediction agreement for the candidate run
any PhysMAP flag, materiality value or detector outcome
any CFD result for the candidate run
class balance, or how many runs a proposed rule would admit
permitted_inputs_when_fixing_the_rules: source-reported operating conditions (Re, Pr, Gr_q, wall BC, geometry)
source-reported energy balance and heat loss
the absolute bulk-temperature error expressed against wall-to-bulk difference
a transition criterion from an INDEPENDENT source, used inside its stated validity range
Lewis's Table 7.1 predicted-reversal list, with its known limitation that a laminar code cannot predict transition
rules_for_the_evaluation_set.note_on_the_last_two: No independent transition criterion currently qualifies. Hallman's was tested and rejected: Lewis's stations lie 1.5x to 24x outside its stated validity range. Until one exists, the flow-eligibility rule cannot be closed, and therefore neither can the evaluation set.

development_vs_evaluation_split.metrics_state: CLOSED, and this ruling does not move that.
development_vs_evaluation_split.no_outreach: Standing. No author contact, no interlibrary request.

cfd_model_requirements.ruling: The constant-property Boussinesq case is retired as the model of record for Lewis. A property basis may NOT be selected because it matches the measurements best.
cfd_model_requirements.required: Variable-property solver using Lewis's OWN Appendix B polynomials, which is what his numerical code used. This removes the basis choice rather than making it.
retained_unchanged: geometry: d = 0.0119 m, heated L = 1.900 m, L/d = 159.66
uniform wall heat flux over the heated length, adiabatic over the entry
Lewis's property definitions (Appendix B equations B.2, B.4, B.5, B.6)
Nu reduced on Lewis's linear energy-balance bulk temperature and inlet-bulk k = 0.5922
cfd_model_requirements.diagnosis_is_not_scoring: These are the burned development runs. Agreement with them is a debugging signal, not a result.
